title: Imaging and analysis on the interaction between human antigen-pulsed Vδ2 T cells and antigen-specific CD4 T cells
protocol: Mix CD4 T cells isolated from pp65-stimulated PBMCs with pp65-pulsed γδ-T cells at a ratio of 1:1 in R10 medium.
Incubate the mixture overnight (around 18 hours) in NuncTM Lab-TekTM II 8-well chambered coverglass.
Culture cells overnight in a NuncTM Lab-TekTM II 8-well chambered coverglass at a density of ~1 million cells per mL and a volume lower than 0.4 mL for cell settling.
Aspirate the media slowly and carefully from top-to-bottom at the bottom-right corner of each well using a 200 μL pipette.
Add 200 μL PBS slowly and gently to each well at the upper-left corner.
Aspirate the PBS slowly and carefully from top-to-bottom at the bottom-right corner of each well.
Add 200 μL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA, dissolved in PBS, pH 7.4) to each well and keep it at room temperature (22°C~28°C) in the dark for 20 min to fix the cells.
Aspirate the 4% PFA and wash with 200 μL PBS twice.
Add 200 μL of Perm/Block buffer and keep the chamber at 4°C for 20 min.
Wash with 200 μL Staining Buffer twice.
Incubate with primary antibodies in 200 μL Staining Buffer at 4°C overnight (~18 h).
Wash cells with 200 μl Staining Buffer twice the next day (Day 2).
Incubate cells with secondary antibodies in 200 μl Staining Buffer at 4°C for 30 min.
Wash cells with 200 μl Staining Buffer twice.
Mount cells by adding 200 μl SlowFadeTM Gold antifade reagent with DAPI and incubate at room temperature (22°C~28°C) in the dark for 30 min.
Perform imaging as soon as possible after IFA is completed to avoid bleaching and obtain clearer signals.
Store the chamber in a dark place at 4°C if confocal microscopy is to be performed later.
Image IFA samples using confocal microscopes such as LSM700, LSM800, or Leica SP 5 II.
Focus on the colocalization of Δ42PD1 signal on Vδ2+ cells and TLR4 signal on CD4 T cells.
Include HLA-DR presence on Vδ2+ cells in the imaging analysis.
Use protein expression on cell-only groups (Groups 1, 2, 3, and 4) as controls for comparison.
Scan at least three images for each group using a 10× lens.
Scan images using a 10× lens for general view and cell identification.
Scan at least five images per chamber using a 40× or 63× oil lens for experimental groups 5, 6, 7, and 8.
Scan at least five Z-stack images for group 8.
Set the first scanning position of the Z-position by decreasing focus height until cell structure is no longer visible.
Increase focus height to set the last scanning position where cell structure is no longer visible.
Adjust pinhole size using the “1 AU” hotkey.
Use optimal frame size and resolution settings recommended by the software.
Follow scan speed recommendations from the software.
